title: Confirm timeout leaves app stuck in confirm mode
detail: ask_confirm raises after 120 s (and execute_actions' confirm op doesn't catch it at all). The brain only sends say('Okay, cancelled'), and AppDelegate.onSay drops it while pendingConfirm != nil. Nothing tells the app the confirm is over, so the confirm bubble stays up with no autoHide, and VoiceController.handleFinal (lines 230-239) treats every later utterance as a yes/no answer, so non-yes/no commands just show confused. Clicking Confirm later sends a reply for an id the brain already dropped; the app shows 'On it.' and sets mood thinking, which sits there until the 45 s safety net. Within a 3-min demo, one slow answer or one stray confirm leaves the agent unusable until someone clicks Cancel.
evidence: reviews/ux/tests/test_confirm_timeout_stuck.py::test_confirm_timeout_clears_app_confirm FAILS: frames sent = [ui thinking, confirm, say 'Okay, cancelled']; no frame that clears pendingConfirm. App side: AppDelegate.swift:112-118 (onSay suppressed while pendingConfirm), VoiceController.swift:230-239.
fix: Brain: on timeout/cancel/exception during ask_confirm send {"t":"confirm","id":cid,"done":true} (or ui idle + new 'confirm_cancel' type; add it to AGENTS.md). Wrap execute_actions' confirm op in try/except RuntimeError like _skill. App: on that frame (and on any ui frame whose mood isn't thinking) clear pendingConfirm and hide the bubble. Also have the app auto-decline after ~60 s itself.

title: Confirm prompt is the catalog description, never names recipient/file
detail: _summary() returns the catalog description, so the confirm for send_message is 'Send an iMessage/SMS to a contact.' and move_to_trash is 'Move a file or folder to the Trash.' Neither shows who, what or which file. The user is approving blind. That defeats CONFIRM, and the demo's signature 'Send the message to Mom?' moment reads as generic. It isn't phrased as a question either. The same text is also sent first as a ui 'thinking' bubble.
evidence: test_confirm_summary_names_object FAILS: summary='Send an iMessage/SMS to a contact.' for args {to:'Mom', body:'hi'}. Catalog: send_message args to/body, move_to_trash arg path, compose_email.
fix: Per-skill confirm templates in catalog.json (e.g. "confirm":"Text {to}: “{body}”?", "Move {path|basename} to Trash?", "Send email to {to}?"). Format with the coerced args and truncate the body to ~40 chars. Fall back to f"{desc.rstrip('.')}?" only when there's no template. Drop the duplicate ui bubble.

title: Skill success shows no reply text; user sees own transcript
detail: _skill ends with ui('success') and no bubble or say. The last thing the bubble showed is the user's own transcript (VoiceController.handleFinal:253 showBubble(text,.transcript)). So for every System-1 command (volume, open app, dark mode, timers: most of the demo) the mascot grins under the user's words and never says 'Opened Downloads'. This breaks the product rule that the mascot replies in the bubble with specific copy. The skill result (rpc result) is available but thrown away.
evidence: orchestrator.py:375 `await self.server.ui("success")` only; protocol.ui supports bubble. AppDelegate.onUI shows a bubble only when one is given.
fix: Add a per-skill 'done' template in catalog.json ('Volume {level}%', 'Opened {app}', 'Timer set: {duration|human}', 'Dark mode on') and send ui('success', bubble=template.format(...)) of <=12 words. Prefer the result fields when present (battery_status/todays_agenda need to *show* the result: those are ANSWER-type and currently say nothing at all).

title: Ghost cursor never appears for skills (most demo actions)
detail: For rpc 'skill', RPCHandler calls handsWillAct(op:name, frame:nil). GhostCursor.handsWillAct returns 0 at once when frame is nil and never starts a flight. handsDidAct then calls land(), which is a no-op because landed==true. So open_app, open_folder, web_search, play_music, set_volume (the whole System-1 path) run with no ghost cursor, no highlight and no chip. The 'ghost cursor shows where the agent acts' wow only shows up on planner act ops. The mascot also gets no 'acting' look target.
evidence: GhostCursor.swift:57-62 `guard let frame ... else { return 0 }`; RPC.swift:63 passes frame: nil, label: nil.
fix: For skills with a visible target, pass a frame: the Dock icon of the target app (AX of Dock process, 'AXDockItem' with title == app) for open_app/quit_app/hide_app/play_music (Music); the Finder sidebar row for open_folder; the menu-bar volume/brightness extras for set_volume/mute. Otherwise show a chip-only state next to the mascot ('Opening Safari…') via a new GhostCursor.announce(label:). ~2 h.

title: Offline utterances replay minutes later as surprise actions
detail: When the brain is offline, handleFinal shows 'My brain is offline…' and still queues the final utterance. didOpen flushes up to 3 queued utterances on reconnect, whenever that happens. The user has already been told it failed. Then, at some later point, the agent starts acting on stale commands with no fresh context, several in a row. Each new final cancels the last (server._start_utterance), so only the last one survives, but half-executed earlier ones may already have acted. During the demo, restarting the brain after a hiccup would fire whatever was said while it was down.
evidence: VoiceController.swift:247-251 comment 'queued for reconnect'; BrainConnection.swift:98-100 outbox.append for final utterances; :151-153 flush in didOpenWithProtocol.
fix: Drop the outbox, or keep only entries < 5 s old and, on replay, show 'Back online — doing: <text>' first. Simplest: delete the outbox and change the hint to 'My brain is offline. Try again in a sec.'

title: Utterance frames omit contract ctx (app/focused/selection/online)
detail: AGENTS.md requires the app to capture ctx at push-to-talk key-down, before any Muselet UI. sendUtterance sends only id/text/final, and VoiceController.pressBegan never captures the frontmost app or focused element. The orchestrator ctx stays at {'app':'none',...} forever (orchestrator.py:55-56). The router and arg extractor are trained and evaluated with ctx, so live accuracy on deictic commands ('quit this', 'type hello here', 'copy that') falls to the no-context case, even though it'll look fine in evals.
evidence: BrainConnection.swift:62-64; grep 'ctx' in app/Sources/MuseletApp → no matches; server.py:103-105 also drops msg['ctx'] (on_utterance(text, True)).
fix: In pressBegan (before mascot.wake/showBubble): ctx = {app: NSWorkspace.frontmostApplication.localizedName, focused: AX focused element as '<role> "<label>"', selection: AXSelectedText non-empty, online: NWPathMonitor cached status}. Store it per currentID and attach it to every utterance frame. Brain: pass msg.get('ctx') through on_utterance into orch._ctx.

title: Listening feedback waits on cold AVAudioEngine start
detail: pressBegan calls recorder.start() synchronously and only afterwards sets mood .listening and shows the 'Listening…' bubble. AudioRecorder builds the engine, installs the tap, prepares and starts it on every press ('engine only runs while the key is held'). A cold start of AVAudioEngine input with the mic indicator is typically 100-300 ms on macOS (not measured here: Linux VM). For that time the key-down gets no visible response, and the first syllable is lost because the tap isn't capturing yet. This is the most important time-to-first-feedback number.
evidence: VoiceController.swift:140 `try recorder.start()` precedes :153 `model.mood = .listening`; AudioRecorder.swift:36-56 builds/prepares/starts per press.
fix: Set mood .listening and show the bubble first, then start the recorder on the next runloop turn. Call engine.prepare() once at launch, after mic permission, so start() is cheap. Log keydown→first-buffer ms to FileLog next to stt_latency so it can be measured on the M5.

title: Bubble copy leaks raw skill ids and gives no next step
detail: Users see snake_case internals: 'Did you mean set_volume or change_volume?' (the top-2 might even be MULTI_STEP/ASK), 'send_message didn't work', 'I'm missing some details', 'Script failed'. None of them says what to do next. The real error (e.g. 'contact not found', 'app not installed') is discarded by _fail (raw_error unused, not even traced). Judges will notice these on any miss.
evidence: orchestrator.py:146 f"Did you mean {a} or {b}?"; :369/:374 f"{name} didn't work"; :251-254 _fail ignores raw_error.
fix: Add 'title' per skill in catalog ('set the volume', 'send a message') and use it in the copy. Map common HandsKit errors to next-step copy ('I can't find Mom in Contacts.', 'Safari isn't installed.', 'Grant Automation for Music in Settings.'). Skip special labels in 'Did you mean'. Trace raw_error. Keep it <=12 words.

title: Utterance frames omit contract ctx (app/focused/selection/online)
evidence: fixed in wip/local 1d7cc07: pressCtx = UtteranceCtx.capture() at key-down, sent on partial+final frames; server.py:105 passes msg.ctx -> cli.py:60 -> orchestrator.handle_utterance merges into _ctx. Still open on main 10793e0.

title: Bubble copy leaks raw skill ids and gives no next step
detail: Partly fixed: 'Did you mean' now goes through _human() ('change volume'). Failures still say f"{name} didn't work" (e.g. 'send_message didn't work') and _fail still discards raw_error, so there's no next step.
evidence: orchestrator.py:421,426@1d7cc07 f"{name} didn't work"; _human only used at :151-152.
fix: Use self._human(name) or a catalog title, and map raw_error to next-step copy, as in pass 1.

title: Key-down ctx capture blocks main thread before mascot listens
detail: pressBegan (main thread) calls UtteranceCtx.capture() before model.mood = .listening. capture() makes up to 4 synchronous AX IPC calls into the frontmost app: focused element twice (focusedSummary and hasSelection each re-query it), its attrs, and AXSelectedText. The app-element calls are raw AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue with no AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout, so they use the system default (~6 s), unlike HandsKit's 0.25 s in AX.swift:66. If the frontmost app is busy (Premiere rendering, Chrome with a heavy page, Numbers recalculating), the mascot and PTT tap freeze before any visible listening. Worst case is about 2×6 s, and even a healthy Electron/Chrome app adds tens of ms to the key-down→listening time. It also adds to ux-7.
evidence: VoiceController.swift:142 recorder.start, :154 pressCtx = UtteranceCtx.capture(), :158 mood = .listening @1d7cc07; UtteranceCtx.swift:34-37 and :50-53 AXUIElementCreateApplication + AXUIElementCopyAttributeValue with no setMessagingTimeout; grep MessagingTimeout → only HandsKit Observe/AX.swift. Not timed on device (Linux VM).
fix: Get frontmostApplication synchronously (cheap, and it's what the contract needs before Muselet UI). Do the AX focused/selection lookup on a background queue with AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout(appEl, 0.1), query the focused element once, and attach the result when it's ready (partials can go out without ctx until then). Set mood .listening first.
